what_worked: Revenue-index metric on slide 2 is a genuinely useful original construct with clear chart design.
fix_next: The denominator for category shares uses 1,000 instead of 726 categorized rows, inflating AI to 27% and distorting every index value.
verdict: Clean, focused deck undermined by a denominator error that ripples through its headline insight.
factual_error_detail: Slide 2: '27% of all 1,000 startups building in AI' — AI has 197 of 726 categorized rows (27.1% of categorized, not of 1,000; 274 rows lack category). Using 1,000 as denominator makes AI share 19.7%, and all index ratios are wrong. E-comm share of 1,000 is 1.9% not 2.6%; the 5.15x index is therefore incorrect (correct index using categorized base ≈ revenue-share/startup-share with 726 denominator differs). Slide 2: E-comm revenue share stated as 13.4% — $1,111,606/$15,596,345 = 7.13%, a large overstatement. Slide 3: On-sale median MRR $1,055 vs $187 and 5.6x multiple, and the revenue-multiple distribution percentages are all unverifiable against the frozen reference and appear fabricated. Slide 4: Correlation values (0.87 MRR, 0.55 subscriptions, 0.27 domain rating) are presented without sourcing and cannot be verified; the one verifiable correlation in the reference (founded-year r=0.025) is not tested here.

evidence.insight: The revenue-index concept (slide 2) goes beyond simple description and the vanity-metric debunking (slide 4) is decision-useful, but the marketplace insight (slide 3) is largely descriptive with unverifiable numbers.
evidence.narrative: Three-insight structure with a clear thesis ('where revenue actually lives') and a summary slide that synthesizes into actionable recommendations. Sequence is logical: category → marketplace → predictors → so-what.
evidence.framing: Dataset size and source noted, but 274 missing category values are never disclosed. No limitations section. Audience framing ('for Sritam') is thin — who is Sritam and what decision does this inform? Scope of '30-day revenue' vs 'all-time revenue' used interchangeably without clarity.
evidence.accuracy: Slide 2 uses 1,000 as denominator for category shares when only 726 rows have categories, producing wrong percentages and wrong index values. E-comm revenue share overstated (~7.1% actual vs 13.4% claimed). Slide 3 claims are entirely unverifiable. Slide 4 correlations plausible but unverifiable except directionally.
evidence.visual: Consistent color scheme (teal/orange), clean horizontal bar charts, good use of callout boxes with big numbers. Chart types are appropriate. Legibility is strong. Slight template sameness across slides but not egregious.
evidence.ai_slop: Mild template uniformity across slides with identical layout patterns. The revenue-multiple distribution on slide 3 has the hallmarks of fabricated round-number percentages (34/27/18/13/8). Overall polish is high but some numbers feel generated rather than computed.
